body: @harpone It's only embarrassingly wrong if one is irrationally embarrassed by making mistakes!
@harpone To clarify: by "embarrassingly wrong" all you mean is that it should be `dL/dx = dL/dy dy/dx` to avoid implying that `d/dy` is differentiating `dy/dx`?

Yup, exactly! Was a bit tired yesterday so maybe I overreacted a bit though :)

Anyway, for example the abs + it's gradient would probably make for a better example?
Oops actually maybe `abs` is not a good example, see [this](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/3647) (possible) bug.
@harpone Are you happy with this chain rule fix?  https://github.com/girving/tensorflow/commit/05e7bc317317cc868710db2762acaab87b8c17a4

Sure, that's much better!

It's a nontrivial amount of work for a marginal gain, since the goal of the tutorial is to teach people how to use the API, not to teach them calculus.

I'm afraid I don't have the time right now, but I may submit a PR related
on another thing (log abs det gradient etc.) some time in the future, so I
could also do this in the same PR? No promises however, it could take a
while...
